title: Infra team wiki: GPU fleet, cloud accounts, networking, IaC modules, and CI/CD (comprehensive guide)
author: Aisha Carter
body:
Summary:
This team wiki page consolidates Redwood Inference's infrastructure engineering guidance for GPU fleet capacity planning, cloud accounts and networking, Terraform/IaC module patterns, CI/CD and build pipelines, and operational runbooks. It is intended as the primary reference for infra engineers, platform owners, and on-call SREs.

Scope:
- GPU fleet sizing and SKU recommendations (NVIDIA H100/A100, M60 for legacy)
- Cloud account and VPC organization patterns across AWS, GCP, and Azure
- Recommended Terraform module layout and usage patterns
- CI/CD pipeline templates for infra and model-serving runtime components
- Runbooks for capacity events, maintenance windows, and incident escalation

Ownership and contacts:
- Platform: infra-team-ops (primary)
- GPU fleet capacity: infra-capacity pager rota
- Networking & cloud accounts: cloud-platform
- IaC modules: infra-iac-team
- For urgent issues: oncall@redwood-inference.com (follow oncall rota)

GPU Fleet & Capacity Planning (guidelines):
1) Headroom policy: maintain 25% reserved headroom per region for burst/beta customers.
2) Sizing methodology:
   - Baseline QPS and tokens-per-second per model; use 95th percentile request size for kernel sizing.
   - Convert tokens -> GPU memory/time using per-model perf table (link to perf table in related pages).
   - Plan for sustained throughput + 30% autoscale buffer.
3) SKU recommendations:
   - H100 (4/8/16GB) for largest models and lowest-latency routes
   - A100 for general-purpose production-serving pools
   - T4/A10 for inference-light experimental workloads

Cloud Accounts & Networking (standards):
- Account layout: org-root -> shared-services (idp, logging, monitoring) -> prod -> staging -> dev -> customer-private (when applicable).
- VPC design: one VPC per region per environment; use shared Transit Gateway or VPC Peering for cross-region control-plane traffic.
- Subnet & security: public load-balancers in public subnets; GPU subnets must be private with NAT egress; strict NACLs and security-groups by role.
- Network egress controls: central NAT gateways in shared-services; use egress proxy for model artifacts and kibana access.

Terraform / IaC Modules (patterns):
- Repo layout: 
  - infra-iac/modules/* (reusable modules: network, k8s-cluster, gpu-pool, iam, monitoring)
  - infra-iac/envs/{prod,staging,dev} (composition via modules)
  - infra-iac/pipelines (CI pipeline configs)
- Module patterns: small focused modules, explicit inputs/outputs, avoid implicit provider configs. Version modules with semantic tags (v1.2.0).
- State management: remote state in S3/GCS with locking via DynamoDB/CloudSQL. Use workspace-per-environment pattern for deployments.

Terraform example snippet (usage pattern):
module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infra-iac.git//modules/gpu-pool?ref=v1.3.0"
  region = var.region
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  min_size = var.min_size
  max_size = var.max_size
  tags = var.tags
}

CI/CD & Build (recommended templates):
- Pipelines should be declarative; prefer GitHub Actions or GitLab CI with reusable workflows.
- Gate rules: plan must run on PR, apply only on merged main and from a trusted automation user.
- Secrets: store in KMS-backed secrets manager; pipeline agents must use short-lived credentials (OIDC where supported).
- Example pipeline steps for infra changes:
  1. terraform fmt/check + static checks (tflint, checkov)
  2. terraform init + plan (upload plan artifact)
  3. automated plan review + human approval for prod applies
  4. apply via terraform apply + notify channels (pagerduty/slack)

Build and Image promotion for inference runtime:
- Build images in a central build account, scan images (Snyk/clair), sign artifacts, then replicate to prod registries.
- Use image tags: build-<sha>-<date>, promoted->release-<semver>.

Runbooks (operational procedures):
- GPU capacity spike runbook (short):
  1. Triage: check dashboards (gpu-utilization, queue-depth, tail-latency)
  2. If utilization > 85% sustained: enable emergency autoscale policy (playbook link)
  3. If autoscale fails: evict best-effort workloads, promote reserved capacity, and notify customers via CS
  4. Post-incident: open postmortem, update capacity models

- Maintenance window checklist:
  - Notify stakeholders 72/24/1 hours out
  - Drain serving nodes (cordon & drain for k8s) after warm cache flush
  - Apply infra changes in staging, smoke-test with synthetic prompts, then roll to prod in canary groups
  - Monitor for 60 minutes at 1-minute granularity for error spike

Operational dashboards & SLOs (minimum):
- GPU pool SLOs: fleet availability 99.95% monthly; scheduling latency p95 < 50ms (control plane).
- Serving SLOs: request success rate >= 99.9% ; token latency p95 target as defined per model in model-catalog.
- Alert thresholds: GPU node down (>=1 node) -> P3; sustained GPU util > 90% for 15+ minutes -> P2; queue depth > 1000 -> P1.

Change management & emergency rollback:
- All infra changes require a documented plan in the PR description with risk, rollback steps, and blast radius.
- Rollback strategy: restore from previous module tag and apply; scale up reserved pool; open critical incident channel.

Onboarding checklist for new infra engineers:
1. Access requests: cloud console, infra repos, pager, slack channels
2. Read this team wiki and run through the runbook exercises
3. Pair with an oncall engineer for first 2 oncall shifts

Appendix: Useful commands and links
- Terraform plan (example): 
  - terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-terraform-state"
  - terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
  - terraform show -json plan.tfplan | jq '.'
- K8s drain example: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- Perf tables and model cost calculator: see /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite
- Incident postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/postmortem-template.json

Document maintenance
- Owner: infra-iac-team (email infra-iac@redwood-inference.com)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major incident/capacity event

Notes and references:
- See related modules in infra-iac repo and the perf-suite for model-specific sizing guidance.
- This page is a living document; propose edits via PR to infra-team-wiki repo and notify reviewers.
